A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Pan-LUT for pan-sharpening. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions. v1 ends after the references; v2 includes Appendices A.1–A.8 and a checklist, which were also inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pan-LUT accuracy, inference timings, full-resolution evaluations and component/LUT-size ablations in Sections 4–5.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmarking, CPU/GPU efficiency measurements, component ablations and regularization experiments in Section 4 and the appendix.

M1.justification: v1 adds PGLUT's spectral output to AALUT's aggregation of PAN-only SDLUT outputs. v2 replaces this with serial PGLUT -> SDLUT -> AOLUT processing: intermediate features retain C+1 channels, and AOLUT maps five feature channels to multispectral outputs. Rotation equations also change from parallel outputs to successive transformations. v2 specifies MSE instead of L1 reconstruction loss, although its final loss equations and Appendix A.5 retain conflicting L1 descriptions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate reduced-resolution pan-sharpening on WV2, GF2 and WV3, plus unseen full-resolution WV2 scenes. Additional visualizations and hardware/image-size scaling measurements extend evaluation within this coverage; they introduce no new satellite dataset, population or fusion task.

E2.justification: v2 adds PanNet to Table 1 and seven traditional comparators in Table 7: PCA, Wavelet, GSA, GFPCA, PRACS, AWLP and MTF-GLP-HPM. Its resource comparison also includes GCPNet, SpanConv, LGPConv, PGCU and UAPN-S. DiCNN and SRPPNN points from v1's Figure 1 disappear. Table 2 retains its comparator membership.

E3.justification: Reported training increases from 600 to 1000 epochs, and the initial learning rate changes from 3e-4 to 5e-4. v2 adds CPU timing and maximum-image-size tests on 11GB and 24GB GPUs. Table 1 retains 2K/4K GPU timings but removes the 1K timing column. Wald downsampling, quality metrics, the 200 full-resolution samples and averaging timings over 100 images remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Component ablations expand from four configurations in v1 Table 3 to six in v2 Table 4, including AOLUT alone and PGLUT with AOLUT, reflecting the revised architecture. Appendix A.6 adds separate smoothness- and monotonicity-weight sweeps in Tables 5–6. LUT-size sensitivity remains, with revised results and additional storage accounting.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run or dispersion statement. v2 checklist item 7 newly claims standard deviations over several random runs. However, the displayed tables and plots contain point estimates without those deviations, seeds or a run count. This is an added reporting claim, not demonstrated uncertainty reporting or evidence that more runs occurred.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces Pan-LUT's WV2/GF2/WV3 PSNR values 39.8362/42.6559/28.8213 with 40.8555/43.7466/29.7376 for the revised model and training. Table 2 replaces QNR 0.7985 with 0.8829, moving above the retained TA-DiffHQP value 0.8025. Reported 2K/4K GPU timings change from 0.28/0.30 to 0.38/0.54 ms. Additional baseline, capacity, CPU and ablation results substantially expand the evidence; these are not controlled gains under unchanged model/training settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds an explicit neighborhood-set proof that four rotations cover a 3×3 region from 2×2 neighborhoods; v1 only describes rotation-based receptive-field expansion informally. v2 also adds parameter-count and dimensional storage formulas. This is a localized theoretical addition, and the neighborhood-union argument is not clearly reconciled with the sequential transformations in Equations 5 and 22.

C1.justification: The stated component contribution changes from adaptive aggregation of spatial outputs to AOLUT-based channel aggregation. The abstract and introduction replace the below-300K-parameters/8K submillisecond claim with below 700K parameters and 9K×9K processing, and add 15K×15K processing on a 24GB GPU. The first-LUT-for-pan-sharpening positioning and broad full-resolution superiority claim are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains PAN-guided indexing through discrimination between identical multispectral values with different PAN values. Appendix A.1 newly discusses exponential storage growth with input dimensionality and the capacity/efficiency tradeoff of neural integration. Appendix A.6 interprets excessive smoothness regularization as restricting LUT flexibility. These add specific mechanisms and applicability limits.

D1.justification: Appendices A.2–A.5 substantially expand module input/output specifications, per-channel lookup, interpolation weights and regularization details. v2 also provides LUT parameter accounting, the CPU model and GPU-memory conditions, and a source-code location absent from v1. These are substantial documentation additions; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked code's availability.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds positioning against adaptive convolutions and lightweight pan-sharpening, citing LAGConv, CANConv, SpanConv and LGPConv. The generalization-focused paragraph and several ISP-background citations are removed, while other citations are added. The broad LUT/traditional/deep-learning framing and first-LUT novelty claim remain.

P1.justification: The main narrative and most section ordering are retained, with localized rewrites to motivation, indexing explanations and module descriptions. Adaptive output receives its own subsection, the standalone ablation section becomes Section 4.4, and detailed exposition is organized into new appendices. Author/affiliation information changes and a checklist is added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. Figure 1 replaces the accuracy/speed scatterplot with CPU-time and GPU-capacity comparisons, and Figure 2 is extensively redrawn for the revised pipeline. Tables gain parameter columns and expanded ablations, with new storage, regularization and traditional-comparison tables. The GF2 visualization moves to Appendix Figure 7, and a reduced-resolution WV2 visualization is added.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's efficiency evaluation centered on GPU timing, v2's CPU/capacity tests, broader comparisons and regularization ablations better substantiate the central efficiency and design claims. Explicit limitations and code-access information also help. These gains are tempered by newly conflicting L1/MSE descriptions and a checklist assertion of standard deviations unsupported by the displayed results, leaving a limited net improvement in paper quality.
